children: Partnerships with Nexperia, Fujifilm, Besi, SCL and Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya span wafer fabrication, advanced packaging, materials, indigenisation and talent development

Tata Electronics has signed seven memorandums of understanding (MoUs) at SEMICON India 2026, expanding partnerships across semiconductor manufacturing, materials, advanced packaging, supply-chain localisation and talent development as the Tata group company builds its semiconductor manufacturing footprint in India.

The agreements announced on Thursday include partnerships with Dutch chipmaker Nexperia, Japan's Fujifilm, Dutch semiconductor equipment maker Besi, government-run Semiconductor Laboratory (SCL) and Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya.
Tata Electronics CEO and Managing Director Randhir Thakur said the company is also set to sign further agreements at the event, taking the total to 16, according to media reports.

The announcements come as India seeks to develop a broader semiconductor value chain spanning chip design, fabrication, packaging, materials, equipment and workforce development. The government approved ISM 2.0 in July with an outlay of Rs 1.27 lakh crore, expanding support for areas including semiconductor research, design, machinery and materials, fabs, talent and ATMP/OSAT facilities.

Under its agreement with Nexperia, Tata Electronics will explore manufacturing Nexperia's MOSFET portfolio at its planned 300mm semiconductor fabrication facility in Dholera, Gujarat. The partnership also covers assembly and testing of Nexperia's discrete semiconductor products at Tata Electronics' packaging facility in Jagiroad, Assam.

The companies will additionally collaborate on technology development, research and ecosystem initiatives, bringing together Nexperia's expertise in discrete, power and analog semiconductors with Tata Electronics' emerging manufacturing capabilities.

The Dholera partnership could give Nexperia an additional manufacturing pathway as semiconductor companies seek more geographically diversified supply chains. Nexperia interim CEO Stefan Tilger said the agreement would combine the companies' technology and manufacturing capabilities while supporting a more globally balanced manufacturing network.
Tata Electronics is also seeking to localise the materials needed to operate its Dholera fab through a separate agreement with Fujifilm.

Under that MoU, Fujifilm will develop and supply semiconductor materials for the facility and work with Indian chemical manufacturers on the production of high-purity chemicals. Fujifilm plans to invest about Rs 800 crore, or roughly USD 83 million, in phases to establish a semiconductor materials plant in the Dholera Special Investment Region.

The materials partnership is intended to reduce dependence on overseas supplies of critical fabrication inputs and establish suppliers closer to Tata Electronics' first commercial fab. Fujifilm said its semiconductor materials business is a key growth area and that it sees India's expanding semiconductor market as an opportunity for further growth.

Tata Electronics is investing Rs 91,000 crore, or about USD 11 billion, in the Dholera fab, which is planned to manufacture chips on 28nm to 110nm process technologies for automotive, consumer electronics, computing and data storage, wireless communications and AI applications.

At the back end of the semiconductor chain, Tata Electronics has partnered with Besi to develop advanced packaging capabilities at its Jagiroad facility, where the company is investing USD 3 billion in what it has described as India's first indigenous semiconductor packaging facility.

The Besi agreement covers advanced packaging equipment and technology, technical collaboration and development of the local equipment-support ecosystem. The companies will also explore training, certification and knowledge-sharing programmes for Tata Electronics employees and work on a joint technology roadmap.

The partnership comes as advanced packaging becomes increasingly important for integrating chips used in AI and other high-performance applications, while India attempts to establish a domestic OSAT ecosystem.

A fourth agreement with SCL focuses on semiconductor indigenisation. Tata Electronics and the state-run laboratory will explore collaboration in chip design services, process technology and technology-node enablement, supply-chain localisation and workforce development.
The companies said the collaboration could support projects for government and startups and expand semiconductor capabilities for aerospace, defence, strategic and emerging technology applications.
The fifth announced agreement, with Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, focuses on the workforce needed to construct and operate semiconductor facilities.

Tata Electronics, together with L&T EduTech and Jacobs Solutions, will work with the university on curriculum development, joint certification and industry-oriented training in semiconductor facility engineering, infrastructure systems, project management, logistics and supply-chain operations.
